behaviors.protocol_context: One configured replica and ordered ballot
behaviors.trigger: Heartbeat timeout or try_become_leader; Prepare reception
implementation_guards: handle_leader requires ballot greater than both leader_state ballot and persisted promise. Prepare requires greater promise, or equal promise during Recover.
writes: Self leadership resets LeaderState; flushes batch; stores promise; inserts own Promise; enters Prepare. Received Prepare flushes batch, persists promise, enters follower Prepare, resets sequence and caches Promise.
external_effects: Queues Prepare or Promise through caller-drained outgoing messages.
important_branches: BLE recovery starts own ballot at recovery round when a nondefault promise was recovered. Election selection alone does not establish a prepare quorum.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Prepare quorum and compatible history are required before new acceptance.

unknowns: Configuration identity differs between derived Ballot equality and ordering; outer SequencePaxos routing applicability remains unestablished.

behaviors.protocol_context: Current leader ballot in Prepare, then Accept
implementation_guards: Promises occupy per-node slots; matching ballot and prepare quorum required before transition.
reads: Accepted-round and accepted-index ordering of Promise metadata; maximum decided index.
writes: Installs maximum promised log synchronization atomically with accepted round and decided index; adds buffered proposals/stopsign only if no accepted StopSign; enters Accept.
external_effects: Sends AcceptSync with per-follower session and common-prefix choice. Late same-ballot Promise in Accept replaces follower metadata and sends another AcceptSync.
existing_protections: New leader resets old accepted indexes; highest accepted round and longest prefix within it determine selected suffix.
unknowns: Delayed Promise and AcceptSync interaction during repeated same-ballot recovery needs history-level investigation.

behaviors.trigger: Local/forwarded append, batch flush, AcceptSync, AcceptDecide or AcceptStopSign
implementation_guards: Append rejects accepted reconfiguration. AcceptDecide and AcceptStopSign require matching promise, follower Accept and expected sequence. AcceptSync requires matching promise and follower Prepare.
writes: Leader persists append and updates own accepted index when a batch flushes. Follower synchronizes or appends, flushes as needed, and reports accepted index. StopSign occupies an accepted position.
external_effects: AcceptDecide/AcceptStopSign and Accepted messages; AcceptSync may forward buffered proposals.
important_branches: A buffered append may not immediately persist or send; periodic flush is a separate trigger.

cross_activity_effects.A2: All normal follower writes are qualified by persisted promise and phase.

implementation_guards: Leader requires matching ballot and Leader/Accept; counts per-node accepted indexes at least the proposed index. Follower requires matching promise, Accept phase and expected sequence.
writes: Leader increases decided index only with accept quorum; follower advances decided index and flushes if necessary, capped at accepted index in that branch.
external_effects: Decision is piggybacked on queued AcceptDecide or sent as Decide.
unknowns: Accepted indexes are assigned rather than maximized; legal response ordering and consequences of regression remain unread.

behaviors.trigger: Construction with saved promise; reconnected; invalid sequence; resend timeout
writes: Recovery enters follower Recover and sends PrepareReq; leader resets that peer promise and sends Prepare. Sequence gaps initiate recovery, old sequences are ignored.
external_effects: Timers resend Prepare, cached Promise, PrepareReq and StopSign acceptance/decision as phase permits.
important_branches: Ordinary AcceptDecide/Accepted/Decide are not generally retried by these timeout handlers; transport reconnection and sequence gaps are alternative recovery mechanisms.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Resynchronizes follower before rejoining accepted-prefix support.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Persisted promise qualifies which preparation can be accepted.

unknowns: Caller network delivery and reconnect obligations under silent last-message loss need contract investigation.

writes: Loads cache from stored promise, accepted round, decided index, compaction, log length and StopSign. Sync commits round, decision and optional suffix/snapshot/StopSign via write_atomically.
important_branches: MemoryStorage implements in-memory operations; persistent backend internals remain unread. Failed storage calls panic at protocol callers.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Supplies accepted and decided history for prepare and application.

implementation_guards: Validates nonzero configuration ID, more than one node, local PID inclusion/nonzero and quorum size overlap/ranges.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Quorum thresholds determine promise and accepted-prefix eligibility.

external_effects: Returns copied entries tagged Decided iff their index is below decided index, or compacted/StopSign representations. Application state transfer into a new configuration is caller-owned.
append admits or rejects a proposal; leader prepares/batches, follower forwards, or node buffers when leader is unknown. Caller drives tick and message transfer then reads decisions.

facts.meaning: Replica has recorded a promise ballot that qualifies subsequent protocol messages.
facts.validity_context: Current stored promise; normal same-instance protocol messages compare against it.
facts.durability: Persisted via selected Storage; MemoryStorage alone is not crash durable.
facts.recovery: Construction reads promise and enters Recover when storage returns Some.

facts.meaning: Replica reports an accepted prefix length for a ballot; the leader retains per-node reported lengths for its current ballot.
facts.validity_context: Accepted history is selected and resynchronized across ballots; reports count only at a matching leader ballot in Accept.
facts.durability: Replica prefix persists through Storage; leader aggregation is volatile.
facts.recovery: Prepare selects highest accepted round and longest corresponding prefix before new acceptance.

facts.meaning: Local state records a decided prefix boundary used to classify application reads.
facts.validity_context: Current local storage/cache state; established from quorum formation or qualified leader synchronization/decision.
facts.recovery: Reloads stored boundary; prepare/sync propagates selected decided history.

surfaces.reason: BLE reply admission checks configuration ID, while SequencePaxos dispatch has no visible equivalent and ballot ordering omits config_id. Determine caller instance-routing obligations and whether delayed old-configuration messages can legally reach a new instance.

Completion checks assigned index <= decided before ballot supersession. Determine whether assignment producer, event ordering or prior draining guarantees this is the same entry after authority changes, including late Assigned messages.
Accepted-index vector spans max_pid rather than configured nodes; determine whether sparse legal node IDs cause trim eligibility to include unused zero slots.

formation.explanation: Proposals are buffered/forwarded or accepted by the leader. A new leader first gathers per-node Promises in its ballot, chooses highest accepted round and longest corresponding suffix, and synchronizes a prepare quorum history. In Accept, flushed local writes and qualified follower Accepted reports populate per-node prefix lengths. The leader advances decided only after an accept quorum and propagates Decide or piggybacked decision. Followers require promised ballot, phase and sequence, and storage reads classify entries below the local decided boundary for consumption.

context.explanation: Caller-driven BLE ticks select ballots; explicit takeover also invokes handle_leader. A strictly newer ballot resets leader aggregation and stores a promise. A follower Prepare may acquire newer authority, or reacquire the same ballot only during recovery. Higher promised ballots reject old messages; accept sequence gaps request recovery and outdated sequences are ignored. Recovery reloads durable context and requests Prepare. Decided StopSign seals the current log and caller starts a new instance with transferred application history.

connection.explanation: Ballot election is not a decision quorum. Promises and persisted accepted history constrain new leader formation; batching is flushed before promises, old accepted indexes are reset at a new self ballot, and phase/ballot/sequence checks qualify later support. Previously decided boundaries enter Promise metadata and selected sync. Buffered proposals are appended only after preparation and only without accepted reconfiguration; followers forward buffered proposals after sync when no StopSign exists. Same-ballot reconnect resynchronizes a peer using Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync rather than treating it as ready solely from connectivity.

Transport reliability, ordinary-message loss and retry obligations.
core_overview.rationale: Representative formation, authority, storage/recovery and application-consumption paths are traced; local boundary anomalies and deeper backend/runtime paths remain explicit. This map is not correctness or coverage evidence.
